clue.text: Munch, eating a small nut

indicators.note: eating means the munching word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to munch is to chew
S is the usual abbreviation for small (clothing sizes)

explanation.surface: Someone chomps away, swallowing a little nut.
explanation.definitionFit: This kidney-shaped kernel is a well-known edible nut, so the type names it fairly.

clue.text: Obscene programme for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a course is a programme of study or treatment

explanation.surface: A rude TV show broadcast to the viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude or vulgar language is coarse, close in sense to obscene.

clue.text: Erratic cop tormented with sadism

indicators.note: tormented means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue police officer tortures with cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring in fits and starts, irregular, which is what erratic means.

clue.text: Blows out former wife then husband drinks …

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ales are beers, drinks

explanation.surface: The ex-wife, then the husband, drink, and someone breathes out heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out air from the lungs is to blow it out.

clue.text: Charlie, poorer swallowing start of soft soap

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for poorer takes a letter inside it

parts.note: lean times are poor ones, so leaner means poorer

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of soft is used

explanation.surface: Charlie, worse off, gulps down some soft soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a typical example of a substance used for washing dirt away.

clue.text: … left single?

parts.note: one is a single

explanation.surface: Continuing 3 down, the drinking couple leave someone alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 3 down's surface; the whole clue both builds and describes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being left on your own is being solitary, unaccompanied.

clue.text: Like this, when finally sat on horse?

definitions.text: Like this, when finally sat on horse?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the following piece

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of sat is used

parts.note: to horse, or go on horseback, is to ride

explanation.surface: How you end up once seated on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side, the posture of a rider in the saddle.

clue.text: Spot on manuscript appears

parts.note: to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A mark on a manuscript shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the impression of being something is to appear so.

clue.text: Epic poem of perhaps 'Odyssey'

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The Odyssey might be called an epic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical Greece this was a section of an epic poem recited at one sitting.

clue.text: Native American swiftly catches horse's head

indicators.note: catches means the word for swiftly holds a letter inside it

parts.note: apace is an old word meaning swiftly

indicators.note: head means the first letter of horse's is taken

explanation.surface: A Native American rider quickly grabs his horse's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Native American peoples of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Hymn about America facing American abomination

indicators.note: about means the hymn wraps around the abbreviation for America

parts.note: an anthem is a hymn or song of praise
A is also an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A national song about the USA set beside an American, called a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' simply places the second A after the first assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathed or detested is an anathema, a direct synonym of abomination.

clue.text: Fan with no time for act

indicators.note: with no means the time letter is taken out of the word for fan

parts.note: to fan flames is to stimulate them

explanation.surface: A fan, short of time, is ready to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in the sense of pretend or feign is to put on a show of something.

clue.text: PA is tense with anger

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to anger someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: A personal assistant is tense and cross.
explanation.walkthrough: PA reads as a personal assistant but means a public-address system; Tannoy is the British brand name used for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudspeaker public-address system, named after the British company that makes them.

clue.text: Reportedly longs for wife

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for longs for is heard rather than seen

parts.note: if you long for someone you miss them

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone is pining for his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a man's spouse, as in 'the old lady'.

clue.text: Clergyman bound by direct order

indicators.note: bound by means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A priest is obliged to follow a direct order.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican parish priest is a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Dessert in diet unusually generous

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of the phrase are set in a different order

explanation.surface: Pudding on a diet would be an unusually open-handed gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Unselfish, not motivated by personal gain, a sense close to generous-minded.

clue.text: Biting fish catching river insect

indicators.note: catching means the fish takes the river letter inside it

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A biting fish snaps up a river insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, incisive remarks are biting, the same as cutting or keen.

clue.text: Sprout puree on jumper missed opening

parts.note: mush is a soft pulpy mass, like puree
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of missed is taken

explanation.surface: Puree spilt on a sweater missed the neck hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater; it is a kangaroo. 'on' is a link word placing pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout up suddenly and grow rapidly is to spring up the way fungi do.

clue.text: Awkward and formal once but relaxed

indicators.note: relaxed means the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone once stiff and formal has now loosened up, yet is still awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill at ease in a situation is a common synonym of awkward.

clue.text: US state's protecting Republican force

indicators.note: protecting means the state's name surrounds a letter

parts.note: Maine is a US state, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: A US state guards its Republican fighting force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marines are a military fighting body, a force of soldiers serving at sea.

clue.text: Bishop inclined — one's given English name?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
apt means inclined, likely to
one is I, and one's gives I plus the S

explanation.surface: A bishop seems willing to bestow an English name on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen a child is to give it a name during the ceremony.

clue.text: Expressionless girl embraced by heartless bloke

indicators.note: embraced by means the girl goes inside the shortened bloke
heartless means the middle letter of the word for bloke is removed

parts.note: a guy is a bloke, a man
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl held by an unfeeling man looks blank.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank glazed stare is glassy, without any expression.

clue.text: Capital haunt's empty around old inn

indicators.note: around means the shell of haunt goes round the next pieces
empty means haunt loses its inside letters, keeping only the outer two

parts.note: a bar is a pub or inn

explanation.surface: The capital's favourite haunt is deserted, surrounding an old pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of Tasmania, the Australian island state.

clue.text: Cool source of babbling brook

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of babbling is taken

parts.note: a rill is a small stream, a brook

explanation.surface: A cool spring feeds a babbling brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' is not chilly here but slang for excellent; brill is British slang, short for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British praise meaning excellent or great, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Sultry redhead seen in local

indicators.note: seen in means one letter is placed within the word for local

parts.note: topical can mean confined to one area, as in a topical cream
the head of red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A sultry redhead spotted down the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a British pub, but here it means restricted to one area.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot and humid weather like that of the tropics is described as sultry.

clue.text: Scarce record album initially by Queen turned up

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of record and album are taken
in a down clue turned up means the piece is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A rare Queen album, first pressing, has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band but stands for ER. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found is uncommon, a plain synonym of scarce.

clue.text: Later on I fancy Chinese, possibly

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so these letters are dressed up anew

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they might like a Chinese takeaway later.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese is one example of an Eastern people or style, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: Medical containers restricting temperature for organs

indicators.note: restricting means the containers hold the temperature letter in

parts.note: vials are small bottles for medicines

explanation.surface: Specimen bottles kept chilled for transplant organs.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's vital organs are informally called this, the heart, lungs and so on.

clue.text: Sweet product, Polo centre, consumed by loads

indicators.note: consumed by means the middle letters go inside the word for loads

parts.note: masses means loads, a great many

indicators.note: centre means the middle letters of Polo are taken

explanation.surface: Loads of people munch the middles of Polo mints, a sweet product.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is a British brand of mint with a hole in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick dark syrup produced when sugar is refined, so a sweet product.

clue.text: Guard posted next to railway

parts.note: posted means sent, as with a letter

explanation.surface: A guard is stationed beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier keeping watch at a post is a guard, the plain synonym.
